monuments.name: Temple of the Obelisks
monuments.description: Sacred hypaethral courtyard containing 26 limestone standing obelisks (baetyls) dedicated to Resheph, elevated central sanctuary podium, and bronze votive figurine deposits.
monuments.provenanceNote: Excavated by Maurice Dunand; famously relocated stone-by-stone 100 meters east to reveal the underlying Early Bronze Age L-Shaped Temple.

monuments.name: Earlier L-Shaped Temple
monuments.description: Lower stratigraphic temple stratum displaying the archaic asymmetric L-shaped ground plan preceding the Obelisk Temple, demonstrating deep urban religious continuity.
monuments.provenanceNote: Stratum underlying the Temple of the Obelisks; preserved as an excavated archaeological exposure.

monuments.name: Ahiram Sarcophagus & Epigraphy Pavilion
monuments.description: Monumental royal sarcophagus resting on four recumbent carved lions, decorated with a banquet frieze, featuring the earliest fully developed 38-word linear Phoenician alphabetic inscription.
monuments.provenanceNote: Discovered in Tomb V of Byblos Royal Necropolis by Pierre Montet in 1923; permanent centerpiece of National Museum of Beirut.

monuments.name: Ancient Bronze Age Harbour & Quays
monuments.description: Ancient natural cove fortified with stone breakwaters, loading quays for Lebanon cedar beams bound for Old Kingdom Egypt, and moored merchant galleys (*gauloi*).
monuments.provenanceNote: Historically attested in Egyptian Old Kingdom Palermo Stone and contemporary archaeological harbor soundings.

monuments.name: Pre-332 BCE Island Citadel & Sea Walls
monuments.description: Formidable offshore island fortress surrounded by multi-tier marine defensive walls engineered with interlocking limestone headers to absorb wave energy.
monuments.provenanceNote: Reconstructed from underwater marine survey data and Neo-Assyrian relief depictions.

monuments.name: Tyre Twin Harbors (Sidonian & Egyptian)
monuments.description: Two complementary all-weather ports: northern Sidonian port protected from Mediterranean squalls, and southern Egyptian port facing south toward the Nile delta.
monuments.provenanceNote: Identified through sediment cores and underwater masonry surveys directed by Poidebard and modern geoarchaeologists.

monuments.name: Alexander's Mole & Tombolo Geology Exhibit
monuments.nativeName: سد الإسكندر وتشكل البرزخ الرملي الجيولوجي
monuments.description: Interactive demonstration illustrating how Alexander's 60-meter-wide military causeway trapped longshore sand drift, transforming offshore island Tyre into a peninsula.
monuments.provenanceNote: Proven by stratigraphic cores proving 30 million cubic meters of sand accumulated against the Macedonian mole.

monuments.name: Sanctuary of Eshmun & Monumental Podium
monuments.description: Massive terraced stone sanctuary at Bostan esh-Sheikh built by King Bodashtart, featuring natural healing water conduits and ritual ablution pools.
monuments.provenanceNote: Excavated by Dunand and Contenau; notable for Phoenician dedication inscriptions carved into inner foundation blocks.

monuments.name: Empty Throne of Astarte
monuments.description: Monolithic stone throne flanked by winged sphinxes; deliberately left empty representing aniconic divine presence in Phoenician religious custom.
monuments.provenanceNote: Unearthed in the Eshmun sacred precinct; descriptive cultural presentation without religious worship mechanics.

monuments.name: Byrsa Acropolis & Punic Fortifications
monuments.nativeName: أكروبوليس تل بيرصا وأسوار قرطاج البونية
monuments.description: Hilltop acropolis commanding the Gulf of Tunis, featuring high-density multistory Punic apartments and fortified defensive bastions.
monuments.provenanceNote: French archaeological mission led by Serge Lancel; uncovered deep pre-146 BCE Punic domestic strata beneath Roman forums.

monuments.name: Magon Quarter & Opus Africanum Architecture
monuments.nativeName: حي ماغون السكني ونظام البناء الإفريقي
monuments.description: Coastal residential sector demonstrating grid planning, central courtyard peristyle houses, rainwater cisterns, and distinctive Opus Africanum timber/stone pier framing.
monuments.provenanceNote: Excavated by German Archaeological Institute; key evidence for sophisticated Punic municipal hygiene and architecture.

monuments.name: Punic Cothon (Circular Military Naval Basin & Commercial Port)
monuments.nativeName: كوتون قرطاج (الميناء العسكري الدائري والميناء التجاري)
monuments.description: Masterwork of ancient naval engineering: outer rectangular merchant port linked to inner circular naval basin with central Admiral's island sheltering slipways for 220 warships.
monuments.provenanceNote: Thoroughly documented by the UNESCO British Carthage Mission directed by Henry Hurst.

monuments.name: Tophet Archaeological Stelae Gallery
monuments.period: Archaic to Late Punic (c. 8th – 2nd century BCE)
monuments.description: Respectful, non-graphic educational gallery displaying carved votive stelae with the Symbol of Tanit and caduceus, presenting archaeological debate between religious sacrifice and infant mortality cemetery.
monuments.provenanceNote: Strictly non-graphic archaeological analysis conforming to child safety and epistemic integrity policies.

monuments.name: Motya Submerged Causeway to Birgi
monuments.nativeName: طريق موتيا المغمور نحو برغي الصقلية
monuments.description: 1.7 km stone road built just under water level across the shallow Stagnone lagoon, enabling wheeled wagon transit to mainland Sicily while remaining invisible to enemy warships.
monuments.provenanceNote: Submerged beneath 40 cm of water today; surveyed by Tusa and Whitaker.

monuments.name: Motya Kothon & Sacred Sacred Pool
monuments.description: Rectangular stone-lined basin connected to the sea by a narrow channel; interpreted as a dry dock / naval repair basin or a monumental freshwater sacred pool dedicated to Melqart.
monuments.provenanceNote: Excavated by Lorenzo Nigro (Sapienza University) revealing freshwater springs within the basin.
